name: Doublelift
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first LCS championship title with Counter Logic Gaming at the 2015 NA LCS Summer Split playoffs at age 22, later winning multiple LCS titles with TSM and Team Liquid before age 26.
early_history_summary: Doublelift started playing console games before moving to DotA, World of Warcraft, and Heroes of Newerth, eventually transitioning to League of Legends. He was recruited by CLG founder HotshotGG as a substitute support player in 2011, and his parents kicked him out of their home over his gaming career choice, leaving him briefly homeless before he committed fully to professional play.
family_context_summary: Born to a Chinese-American family in California; parents strongly opposed his gaming career and kicked him out of the house in 2011 over his decision to pursue professional esports, leaving him briefly homeless.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were not involved in gaming or esports.
primary_early_advantage_tags: family conflict, homelessness, all-in commitment, early LoL competitive scene, CLG recruitment
evidence_summary: Doublelift was kicked out of his family home at age 18 for pursuing professional gaming, becoming briefly homeless before committing fully to esports. He was recruited by CLG founder HotshotGG and gained early exposure through Epik Gamer at DreamHack Summer 2011. His parents' opposition and his lack of a safety net created an urgency that drove his all-in commitment to professional League of Legends. He won his first LCS title with CLG in 2015 and went on to win multiple titles with TSM and Team Liquid, becoming the player with the most LCS championships.
starting_point: Born to a Chinese-American family in California; parents opposed his gaming career and kicked him out at age 18, leaving him briefly homeless.
current_position: Content creator and streamer; plays for his own team Near Airport; widely considered one of the greatest NA LCS players with 8 LCS titles.

early_history_summary: Dyrus began playing League of Legends in its beta phase, achieving rank 1 with Singed. He started his competitive career as support for All or Nothing, then joined Epik Gamer as top laner, gaining exposure through Twitch streaming before being recruited by TSM in 2012.
family_context_summary: Born in Honolulu, Hawaii; mother is Chinese-American and father is British-American. His father wanted him to work for the family plumbing business, but Dyrus pursued professional gaming against his father's wishes.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a plumber who wanted Dyrus to join the family plumbing business; no gaming or esports background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: beta player, rank 1 Singed, early Twitch streamer, TSM gaming house, WCG champion
evidence_summary: Dyrus was an early adopter of League of Legends, playing in the beta phase and achieving rank 1 with Singed. He gained exposure through Twitch streaming while on Epik Gamer, which led to his recruitment by TSM in 2012. He moved into the TSM gaming house in New York to pursue full-time gaming. His father opposed his career choice, wanting him to join the family plumbing business. With TSM, Dyrus won 3 NA LCS titles and the 2011 WCG championship before retiring after the 2015 World Championship.
starting_point: Born in Honolulu, Hawaii to a Chinese-American mother and British-American father; father was a plumber who wanted Dyrus to join the family business.

The myRevenge squad was then picked up by Fnatic, with whom he won the Season 1 World Championship at DreamHack.

His mother encouraged him to get into video games and sometimes played with him, but demanded he complete his secondary education and baccalauréat before pursuing esports professionally. He joined Team Vitality in October 2018 after finishing his education.

evidence_summary: dev1ce grew up in Vejle, Denmark, playing video games with his brother from a young age. He was also a talented badminton player but chose gaming. Denmark has one of the strongest Counter-Strike ecosystems in the world, and dev1ce benefited from the Danish CS pipeline, starting with Copenhagen Wolves in 2013 before moving to Dignitas, TSM, and co-founding Astralis in 2016. He formed one of the longest-standing player trios in CS:GO history with dupreeh and Xyp9x, lasting over 7 years. With Astralis, he won 4 Majors including 3 consecutive, and was named Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2020. His consistent high-level performance since 2014 established him as one of the greatest CS:GO players of all time.

He also founded Games Academy, a Brazilian esports organization, and started his own brand of gaming computers and equipment.
